newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Duma overrules Yeltsin veto on war booty.
newsitem.headline: Russian Duma overrules Yeltsin veto on war booty.

text.p: Russia's communist-dominated lower house of parliament voted on Friday to overrule President Boris Yeltsin's veto on a bill asserting Russian ownership of art treasures seized from Nazi Germany during World War Two.
In all 308 State Duma deputies voted for the motion, just above the 300 votes -- or two-thirds majority of the house -- needed to override a presidential veto. Fifteen voted against.
The original bill, first passed by the Duma two months ago, caused outrage in Germany. Political leaders there have been lobbying hard for the return of the artworks.
The motion now passes to the Federation Council (upper house), where a two-thirds majority is also needed to overturn the veto.

If the Council, which also heavily supported the original bill, does override the veto, Yeltsin will have to sign the law, making all art treasures brought to the Soviet Union as a result of World War Two the inalienable property of the Russian state.
The Kremlin may, however, ask Russia's Constitutional Court to look into the matter.
Yeltsin vetoed the bill on March 18, saying the document breached international law.

He told the Federation Council that parliament's decision would damage Russia's position in talks with west European states, particularly Germany but also France and Poland, whose citizens were robbed by the Nazis and then found their valuables in Soviet hands.

The bill was criticised by both the Russian and German governments. Germany has demanded the return of the artefacts, which include many priceless paintings as well as golden treasures from Heinrich Schliemann's excavations at Troy in the 19th century.

Many Russians view the treasures, seized from museums and homes in Nazi Germany, its allies and occupied countries, as compensation for the wartime suffering of the Soviet people and for the many Russian treasures destroyed in the German invasion.
